title: Classification of Matter
seo_title: Grade 10 Physical Sciences: Classification of Matter Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_code: Grade 10 Physical Sciences: Matter and classification
standard_text: Matter is classified as mixtures (homogeneous and heterogeneous) or pure substances (elements and compounds); materials are described by their properties: metals, non-metals and metalloids, electrical and thermal conductors and insulators, and magnetic and non-magnetic materials. Names and formulae of substances. (summary of CAPS Physical Sciences, Grade 10, Chemistry: Matter and classification)
meta_desc: Free Grade 10 Physical Sciences worksheets (CAPS): mixtures and pure substances, elements and compounds, metals and non-metals, conductors and insulators, and names and formulae. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Matter is a mixture or a pure substance.
key_sub: Pure substances are elements or compounds.
body_html:
How to think about it

A mixture has two or more substances that are not chemically joined; it can be separated by physical methods. A homogeneous mixture (such as salt water) is the same throughout; a heterogeneous mixture (such as sand in water) is not.

A pure substance has a fixed composition. An element has only one kind of atom; a compound has two or more elements chemically bonded in a fixed ratio, such as H₂O. Metals are shiny, malleable and conduct heat and electricity; metalloids such as silicon have properties of both metals and non-metals.

Example

Is air an element, a compound or a mixture?

Its gases are not bonded together.

Answer: a homogeneous mixture

Example

Is carbon dioxide an element or a compound?

CO₂ has two kinds of atom bonded together.

Answer: a compound

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a compound is the same as a mixture.
  • Thinking all metals are magnetic (only iron, cobalt and nickel are).
  • Thinking a solution is a pure substance.

faq.q: How can you separate a mixture?
faq.a: By physical methods such as filtration, evaporation, distillation and chromatography.

items.q: Lethabo lists changes in the kitchen. Which is a chemical change?
c: a cake batter bakes into a cake
water boils and turns to steam
items.e: A new substance with new properties forms.

items.q: Fatima observes that a glass bottle breaks. Is this a chemical change or a physical change?
c: a physical change, because no new substance forms
a chemical change, because a new substance forms
a chemical change, because it looks different
items.e: The substance is still the same; only its shape, size or state changed.

items.q: What is the formula of lithium oxide?
items.e: Li<sup>+</sup> and O<sup>2−</sup>: the charges must balance, so the formula is Li<sub>2</sub>O.

items.q: What is the name of CaO?
items.e: Name the metal, then the non-metal with -ide. Ionic names do not use prefixes.

items.q: Nadia lists changes around the house. Which is a physical change?
c: a cake batter bakes into a cake
bicarbonate of soda and vinegar fizz and make a gas
butter softens in a warm room
items.e: The substance stays the same.

items.q: What is the name of SrO?
items.e: Name the metal, then the non-metal with -ide. Ionic names do not use prefixes.

items.q: Liam lists changes around the house. Which is a physical change?
c: food is digested in the stomach
chocolate is melted and poured into a mould
an apple slice turns brown in the air
items.e: The substance stays the same.

items.q: What is the formula of potassium nitride?
items.e: K<sup>+</sup> and N<sup>3−</sup>: the charges must balance, so the formula is K<sub>3</sub>N.

a chemical change, because a new substance forms
a physical change, because no new substance forms
items.e: The substance is still the same; only its shape, size or state changed.

items.q: What is the formula of lithium fluoride?

items.q: What is the name of MgO?
items.e: Name the metal, then the non-metal with -ide. Ionic names do not use prefixes.

items.q: Which is a characteristic property that can help identify water?
items.e: Density, melting point and boiling point do not depend on the amount, so they help identify a substance.

items.q: What is the formula of calcium nitride?
items.e: Calcium forms Ca<sup>2+</sup> and nitrogen forms N<sup>3−</sup>; the charges must add to zero.

items.q: Precious observes that a glow stick is bent and starts to glow. Is this a chemical change or a physical change?

a physical change, because it is a mixture
a physical change, because only the shape or state changes
items.e: Gas, colour change, new smell, light, heat or a new solid are signs of a new substance.

items.q: What is the formula of calcium oxide?

items.q: Nadia lists changes in the kitchen. Which is a chemical change?
c: a piece of paper is cut into strips
items.e: A new substance with new properties forms.

items.q: Li<sup>+</sup> and N<sup>3−</sup> ions combine. What is the formula of the compound?
items.e: Use the lowest numbers that make the total charge zero: 3 × (+1) + 1 × (−3) = 0.

items.q: A material changes from solid to liquid at 1 538 °C. Which physical property is being described?
items.e: This is the melting point of the material.

items.q: A polymer chain is made of 1 000 units of ethene (C₂H₄, 28 g/mol). About what is its molar mass?
Which is more reactive, lithium (Li) or potassium (K)?
items.e: Alkali metals get more reactive down the group (easier to lose 1 electron).

items.q: A polymer chain is made of 2 000 units of styrene (C₈H₈, 104 g/mol). About what is its molar mass?
Which has the higher melting point: sodium or lithium?
items.e: Melting points of Group 1 metals decrease down the group.

items.q: What is the bond angle in AlCl<sub>3</sub>?
items.e: 3 bonding pairs, 0 lone pairs. Lone pairs repel more than bonding pairs, so each lone pair closes the angle by about 2,5°.

items.q: Why does diamond have a very high melting point?
c: many strong covalent bonds must be broken
items.e: Diamond is a giant covalent (macromolecular) structure.

items.q: Which property makes copper suitable for electrical wiring?
c: it is a good conductor and is ductile
it has a low melting point
items.e: Metals can be drawn into wires.

items.q: Which has the higher melting point: rubidium or sodium?
items.e: Melting points of Group 1 metals decrease down the group.

items.q: How can ethanol be separated from water?
c: fractional distillation, because their boiling points are different
items.e: Ethanol boils at 78 °C, water at 100 °C.

items.q: Which family does calcium (Ca) belong to?
items.e: Group 2 is the alkaline earth metals.

items.q: Why is an alloy usually harder than the pure metal?
c: atoms of different sizes disrupt the layers so they cannot slide easily
items.e: Bronze and steel are harder than copper and iron.

items.q: Which element has chemical properties most like neon (Ne)?
items.e: Same group = same number of valence electrons.

items.q: What is iodine like at room temperature?
items.e: Down Group 17 the colour darkens and the state changes from gas to liquid to solid.

items.q: What is electronegativity?
c: the number of bonds an atom forms
the energy to remove an electron
the power of an atom to attract the pair of electrons in a covalent bond
items.e: Fluorine is the most electronegative element.

items.q: Which family does lithium (Li) belong to?
items.e: Group 1 is the alkali metals.

items.q: Which is more reactive, iodine (I) or chlorine (Cl)?
items.e: Halogens get less reactive down the group (harder to gain 1 electron).

items.q: Which family does krypton (Kr) belong to?
items.e: Group 18 is the noble gases.

items.q: Many glucose monomers are linked in a long chain. Which polymer forms?
items.e: Polymers are chains of repeating monomers.

items.q: Which has the higher melting point: potassium or lithium?
items.e: Melting points of Group 1 metals decrease down the group.

items.e: Xenon is in group 18.

items.q: What is a nanomaterial?
